## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve had to deal with it for so long. Before you make a final decision, could we talk tomorrow—or even tonight if you want? Maybe taking a day or two to think, checking your finances, and considering whether there’s a way to change teams, take leave, or set boundaries would help. But you don’t have to keep suffering just to prove anything. I’ll support you whatever you decide.

## 2

I understand why some images can seem questionable, especially when they’re edited, compressed, or produced by different agencies. But the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn’t depend on photographs alone. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible from different latitudes, Earth casts a round shadow during lunar eclipses, and time zones follow naturally from a rotating globe. Satellites, GPS, long-distance flight routes, and independent observations by people around the world also rely on the same model. Those lines of evidence all reinforce one another, so faking a few photos wouldn’t explain the broader evidence.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than most of the other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from all across the sky.

At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere. A lot of the blue light gets scattered away before the sunlight reaches us, leaving more reds and oranges— which is why sunsets often look so colorful.

雨下了一整夜，细密的水声敲打着窗玻璃，像有人在黑暗中轻轻低语。街灯被雨幕晕开，昏黄的光落在积水里，随着车轮经过，碎成一片片摇曳的影子。远处偶尔传来汽车驶过的声音，很快又被雨声吞没。屋里只亮着一盏小灯，热茶冒着白雾，窗边的猫蜷成一团。这样的夜晚安静而潮湿，却也让人感到一种被世界温柔包围的踏实。
